doctrine: Core thesis: contracts are the business operating system, not legal formalities. Non-negotiable rule: no contract signed = no work. Use LLC entity (separates personal/business liability). Payment structure: 3-stage (50% retainer non-refundable at signing + 25% at milestone + 25% final before delivery). Retain all copyright/source files by default; client gets licensed final deliverables only. Watermark all previews; clean files released only after full payment clears. Key clauses: Creative Judgment (kills style disputes), Late Arrival (time deducted), Force Majeure, Quote Expiry (14 days), Scope definition (prevents creep), Model Release. Licensing model: rent not sell - same asset licensed to non-competing industries simultaneously (wall art, textiles, stationery = multiple revenue streams from one work). IP buyout pricing separate from service fee (reflects lifetime earning potential). Contract governance: simplicity over legal verbosity (1-page 5-section converts faster than 20-page). Living document approach: update quarterly after every project. Gatekeeping workflow: inquiry → standardized quote → client signature via e-signature tool → retainer payment → calendar date → watermarked previews → final payment → clean file delivery. Contract redlining: negotiate terms before price; firms on copyright protection signal high-value status. Enforcement: first out-of-scope request triggers Services clause reference (contract handles it, no emotional negotiation). Copyright registration at delivery point enables statutory damages. Rush delivery premium add-on (revenue lever). Gallery upsell for remaining selects. Late payment penalties defined in contract.

operating_rules: No contract, no work. No exceptions.
Contract under LLC business entity name, never personal name (liability wall)
Contract is living document - update quarterly based on lessons from engagements
Scope creep is contract failure not client problem - point to Services clause
Finals held until balance cleared - watermark previews, clean files last
Copyright stays with creator always - client receives license only
Creative Judgment clause kills 90% of style/color disputes
Late Arrival clause: time deducted from session if client >45 min late
Quote expiry: quotes valid 14 days only, prevents locking outdated rates
One-page 5-section contract converts faster than 20-page legal document
Retainer is non-refundable and de-risks cash flow on cancellations
Register copyright at point of delivery (enables statutory damages if infringement)
Never transfer source files (RAW, PSD, AI) - finals only unless separate IP buyout
Rush delivery premium (standard delivery free, expedited costs extra)
Force Majeure clause covers illness, weather, emergencies
Late payment penalty defined in contract (percentage or flat fee per week)
Model Release secured at signing, not after delivery
Licensing: category-specific exclusivity (greeting cards =/= all paper), territory limits, time limits (12-18 months)
Right to Review clause: licensee sends proofs before manufacturing
Simplicity closes deals - reduce friction, get signature while lead is hot
